_note: NL-channel style vocabulary: styles Anima reproduces that DO NOT EXIST as booru tags -- studio looks, director hands, era aesthetics, technique phrases. Nothing here is measurable by post count, lift or pulls; the evidence is A/B GENERATION, and every entry records its verdict and where the test came from. ANIMA-ONLY until tested on Illustrious: these work through the Qwen3 text encoder reading plain English plus Anima's NL captions, a channel Illustrious's CLIP largely lacks.
_channel_note: These are NL PHRASES, a different channel from booru tags. 'Ukiyo-e style' testing INEFFECTIVE here does not contradict `ukiyo-e` (684 posts, measured pulls) in style_pool -- the tag channel and the phrase channel are separately alive or dead. Where a booru twin exists it is named in `tag_twin`, and the generator must not emit both phrasings of one concept in one prompt.

_source.method: fixed seed, with/without tag, visual comparison; 108 tags on Anima base
_source.finding: tags combining a distinctive palette with concrete motifs reproduce best; abstract worldview descriptors converge or die -- independently the same rule as 'the model draws what you name'

rejected._note: Tested and found dead or harmful ON ANIMA BASE. 'ineffective' is a dead token; 'misconverted' is WORSE THAN NOTHING -- it changes the image wrongly (Katsuhiro Otomo style does not give you Otomo). 'converged' means the phrase produces the same generic output as its siblings. All are RETEST CANDIDATES on finetunes -- Bismuth Anima may differ.
